_readme: Where `pnpm fetch:images` looks for each work on Wikimedia Commons.
search       the query sent to the Commons search API (namespace 6, files)
commonsFile  an exact file, e.g. 'File:Mona Lisa.jpg' — used as given,
skipping search entirely. Add one to pin anything search
gets wrong, then re-run with --only <id>. Changing a pin is
enough on its own: a scan fetched from a different file is
treated as stale, so --force is not needed to correct one.
note         why a work is awkward, where it is awkward
Run `pnpm fetch:images --dry` first and read the table it prints: search
can return the wrong picture, and a wrong painting under the right label
is worse than no painting at all.
Then run `pnpm fetch:images --pin` once and commit what it writes back
here. It records the exact file it chose for every work, so every run after
it — including every CI run — is a lookup rather than a search. Search
rankings drift, and an exhibition that hangs a different picture next month
is not one you can point people at.
Everything listed here is a work whose original is old enough to be in the
public domain. Reproductions of them are PD-Art in the US and in most of
Europe; the fetcher records the licence Commons states for each file in
data/artworks/{id}/image-credit.json, and the Credits panel shows it.
